palette.role: Evergreen foliage and summer scent in warm, sheltered sectors only.

handedness.basis: Searched again in November 2026 in English, German, Japanese, Chinese and Romance-language terms: no written source gives the direction for this species. The one photograph found that shows stems on canes (Wikimedia Commons, "Trachelospermum jasminoides A.jpg") shows crossings in both senses on a pot-grown, cane-trained plant and settles nothing. Darwin records two other twiners of the same family (Dipladenia) as moving against the sun, which would be right-handed: a family-level hint, not evidence for this species.

attachment.supportNeeds: Warm sheltered microclimate; slender timber members or cables to twine.
attachment.caveat: Twining is the primary mechanism (RHS: needs supporting wires or trellis). Aerial rootlets on damp rough surfaces are reported without citation and cannot be ruled out; if real, it could cling to timber as well as twine.

wood.basis: Inferred, with evidence on both sides. For: the RHS record says pruning group 11 "in early spring", and the RHS guide to that group gives spring pruning to climbers that flower on the current year's growth; it flowers in July and August "usually on short lateral twigs" (Bean, Trees and Shrubs Online). Against: NC State Extension says prune after flowering, the timing normally given for old-wood flowerers. No source states the flowering wood outright. The flowering side shoots arise from older stems, so a hard spring prune would still cost flowers.

monthsUK.basis: Bean (Trees and Shrubs Online): flowers "produced in July and August". Stated in months. The RHS record says "mid to late summer", the same two months.

flowering.display: Very fragrant white flowers; glossy dark leaves often bronze-red in winter.

site.aspect: Warm full sun or partial shade, ideally south or west facing, sheltered from cold winds.
site.soil: Fertile, well-drained; dislikes waterlogging and summer drought.

calendar.note: RHS record: pruning group 11 in early spring. RHS guide: maintenance pruning is rarely needed and is done in spring, thinning out congested, weak or damaged shoots.
RHS guide: mulch once a year, in spring or in autumn, on damp soil, leaving 10 cm clear round the stem. Feeding is optional, in spring.

management.notes: Train and tie on to secondary wire, manage spread, inspect for leaf scorch and dieback after winter.

hazards: The whole plant is poisonous (Flora of China); white latex when cut.

sources.label: RHS: pruning established climbers (pruning groups 11 to 13)
